sentences.text:
All these petitions challenge the judgment dated 23/12/2022 passed by the learned District Judge-6, Nagpur in appeals under Section 81-F of the Maharashtra Municipal Corporations Act,
1949 (for short, "the MMC Act" hereinafter), in which a challenge to a notice dated 11/11/2022 under Section 81 B (1) of the MMC Act was raised and has been rejected.

2. Dr. Anjan De, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the provisions of Section 81 B(1) of the MMC Act cannot be taken recourse to against the lease-holder whose period of lease is yet to expire.

He submits that since the lease was granted somewhere in the year 2008, which was for a period of 30 years and also had a clause of renewal, the period for the same could not be curtailed by exercise of the powers under Section 81 B(1) of the MMC Act.

It is also contended that the respondent is bound by its promise made in the brochure preceding the lease, which indicated that the lease 940. WP 54 of 2023.odt would be a long term lease, renewable and the purpose for grant of the lease was for rehabilitation of the petitioners who were displaced on account of construction of the flyover by accommodating them in the shops constructed underneath it.

He, therefore, submits that considering the terms of the lease and the promise, the principle of promissory estoppel will come into play and the respondent would be estopped from going back on the terms of the lease and terminating the same under any guise whatsoever.
He further submits that looking to the entire position, there is no satisfaction of the Commissioner regarding involvement of any public interest.

There is no technical evaluation of the necessity of demolition of the flyover as well as constructing a six lane motorway thereafter, in absence of which, the public interest cannot be presumed to be in existence.

It is also contended that since the petitioners are being deprived of their livelihood,
compensation was required to be granted.

He submits that though a proposal was indicated that a 200 shop complex would be constructed and the petitioners could be accommodated therein, the Bharat Champatrao Khorgade vs Deputy Municipal Commissioner, ... on 14 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/11845736/
2 land on which such complex would be constructed, has not been identified as yet.

sentences.text: It is also contended that considering the undertaking of the Corporation as recorded in Writ Petition No.4331/2002 (pg.253), rehabilitation prior to demolition was a must.

It is also contended that the rehabilitation would indicate making better facilities available and the present facilities which have claimed to be made for the purpose of rehabilitation are only temporary structures, which could only 940.
WP 54 of 2023.odt be termed as pigeonhole, which are unsuitable for rehabilitation and do not satisfy the undertaking given in Writ Petition No.4331/2002.

He further submits that though the scheme for six-lane road was formulated on the basis that the money required for that was already available, however, the same was no longer available, as the said money was already diverted for the works connected with the Futala project (pg.285) and since the funds itself were not available, the entire financial credibility of the project stood crumbled, as a result of which, there was no question of any public interest involved.

It is also submitted that the work was of the Government and not of the Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC), in view of which, it was necessary for the Government to have acquired the land from the NMC by granting suitable compensation to the petitioners who are the lessee of various shop blocks therein under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short, "the Act of 2013").

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He further invites my attention to the definition of "person interested" as occurring in Section 3(x) of the Act of 2013, to contend that the petitioners would be persons squarely covered under the said definition and therefore entitled to compensation.
3. It is also contended that the delegation made by the Commissioner of NMC to the Deputy Commissioner (Property) (pg. 193), as well as the one given to the Assistant 940.

WP 54 of 2023.odt Commissioner, (pg.190), clearly suffered from infirmity as they were not valid under the provisions of Section 49 of the MMC Act and therefore, the notices issued and all actions taken by such persons, in view of such delegation, were clearly infirm.

It is also contended that the delegation by the communication dated 17/11/2020 (pg.189/Clause-7) was for the implementation of a policy, and therefore, did not clothe the Assistant Commissioner with the power to issue a notice under Section 81 B(1) of the MMC Act.

He also contends that since the proviso to Section 49 of the MMC Act has not been shown to have been complied with, the delegation by the communication dated 17/11/2020 (pg.139) was also infirm on that count too, as in absence of its compliance the delegation did not come into effect at all.

4. It is also contended that the material necessary to establish public interest being involved was never placed before the learned District Judge and what was placed before him was only the Resolution dated 29/2/2018 (pg.205) which did not indicate any public interest being involved.

It is further contended that since the minutes of the general body dated 8/9/2021 (pg.209) and the MOU dated 9/12/2022 (pg.281) were documents, which were never placed before the learned District Judge and are coming before this Court for the first time, to supplement the plea of public interest,
in view of what has been held in S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu Vs. Jagannath 1994 AIR (SC) 853 (para 8), the same cannot be looked into,

entities.text: Trimbak Jadhav Vs. State of Maharashtra 2002 (4) Mh LJ 230
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is contended that since the learned District Judge did not frame any point regarding public interest, relying upon Khatunbi Vs. Aminabai 2006 (6) Mh.LJ 759, it is submitted that the matter needs to be remanded back to the learned District Judge for affording an opportunity to the petitioners to meet the plea of public interest as is now being sought to be urged with the help of the additional documents which are for the first time placed on record in these petitions.

It is also contended that the reliance by the learned District Judge on the Bentham Theory was wholly misplaced, as it is an outdated theory and has no applicability in the contextual background of the present petitions, as the action of the respondent intends to deprive the petitioners of their livelihood.

It is also contended that the judgment in Omprakash Vs. Nagpur Municipal 940. WP 54 of 2023.odt Corporation and others 2010 (6) Mh L.J. 700 (para 12) is not applicable to the facts of the present situation, as the position prevailing therein is different inasmuch as in Omprakash (supra), the rehabilitation was being done in the multi- complex being constructed in the same place, in which, certain shops were reserved for the persons, who were displaced, whereas in the instant case the petitioners have been given an offer of shifting to temporary structure which are about 200 meters away from the main road opposite to the railway station, which would add to the loss of business on account of such shifting, apart from which, the premises are not only unhygienic but very dingy also and could only be compared with pigeonholes.

entities.text: Omprakash Vs. Nagpur Municipal 940. WP 54 of 2023.odt Corporation and others 2010 (6) Mh L.J. 700 (para 12)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also places reliance upon the definition of rehabilitation as defined in Merriam - Webster and Collins English Dictionary and submits that there has to be a marked improvement in the conditions than what were in existence earlier for it to be termed as rehabilitation.
5. List the matters tomorrow for the argument of Shri J.B. Kasat, learned counsel for the respondent.
The interim order to continue till tomorrow.
(AVINASH G. GHAROTE, J.)
